residencyRequirements.description: The plaintiff or defendant must have been domiciled or physically present in the State of Hawaii for a continuous period of at least three (3) months immediately preceding the filing of the complaint. The complaint must be filed in the circuit where the plaintiff resides. (HRS §580-1)

waitingPeriod.description: Hawaii has no mandatory waiting period after filing. The court may schedule a hearing at any time after proper service.

noFault.name: Lived Apart for Two or More Years
noFault.description: The parties have lived apart for a continuous period of two or more years under a decree of separate maintenance or by mutual consent

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Differences
noFault.description: There exist irreconcilable differences which have caused the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage

groundsForDissolution.notes: Hawaii is a no-fault only state. The court may grant a divorce on any of the no-fault grounds listed above. (HRS §580-41)

propertyDivision.description: Hawaii courts divide marital property in a just and equitable manner, considering the respective merits of the parties, the relative abilities of the parties, the condition in which each party will be left, the burdens imposed upon either party for the benefit of the children, and all other relevant circumstances.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Property acquired before the marriage or by gift or inheritance may be treated as separate property. However, the court has broad discretion in dividing all property, including separate property, to achieve a fair and equitable result.

legalCitations.description: Grounds for divorce — no-fault only (irretrievably broken, lived apart 2+ years, irreconcilable differences)
Property division and spousal support — fair and equitable distribution
Child custody — best interests of the child; joint custody encouraged
Hawaii Child Support Guidelines — income shares model

filingFees.notes: Hawaii filing fees range from approximately $215 to $265 depending on the circuit. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals.

basic.name: Appearance and Waiver
basic.description: Defendant's voluntary appearance and waiver of service

basic.name: Income and Expense Statement
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, expenses, assets, and debts

basic.name: Decree Granting Divorce
basic.description: Final court decree granting the divorce

service.name: Personal Service
service.description: Service by sheriff, process server, or any adult who is not a party

service.name: Appearance and Waiver
service.description: Defendant waives formal service and enters appearance
service.notes: Must be signed by defendant and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Child Custody and Visitation Plan
withChildren.description: Plan detailing custody and visitation arrangements

withChildren.name: Child Support Guidelines Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per Hawaii Child Support Guidelines (HRS §576E)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Hawaii Family Court filing requirements

inState.description: Defendant must file an answer within 20 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside Hawaii must file an answer within 30 days of service

responseDeadlines.statute: Hawaii Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 12(a)

childSupportGuidelines.description: Hawaii uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Hawaii Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined monthly gross income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust or inappropriate.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Hawaii courts may award spousal support or alimony based on the financial needs of the requesting spouse and the ability of the other spouse to pay, considering the standard of living during the marriage, the length of the marriage, the age and health of the parties, the income and earning capacity of each party, and other relevant factors.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Either party may request spousal support. The court has broad discretion in determining the amount and duration.

court.name: Family Court
court.description: Divorce cases are filed in the Family Court of the judicial circuit where the plaintiff is domiciled. (HRS §571-1 et seq.)
